title: A copy on the canvas says which component it came from
goal: Place copies of a component that has more than one version and each one gets a small marker on the canvas with no words next to it. Three copies of a Save button read as three anonymous dots. The name is in the layers list and the panel, but not where you are looking.
notes:
This is the trade queue/audits/2026-09-08-version-labels.json named itself and asked to be argued with: "A component with two or more drawings no longer shows its name anywhere on the canvas... This is the deliberate trade and it is the first thing to argue with." Reproduced on 2026-09-09 in queue/manager/shots/2026-09-09-0238-three-copies.png: the two originals carry Default and Disabled, the three copies below them carry a bare diamond each.

Putting a name back is not a new control, it is restoring something the width fix took away, so no decision card. If the runner concludes the honest answer is no label at all, dropping the naked marker is an acceptable outcome and should be said plainly in the audit.

Width is the constraint that caused this: read the 2026-09-08 work before re-adding a long string.
acceptance: A copy on the canvas is labelled with something a person can read, or the marker is dropped rather than left saying nothing
Labels still do not cover each other or run into the drawing beside them at 50 percent zoom, which is what the 2026-09-08 version-labels work fixed
To see it: Scripts/probe-app.sh then Scripts/playtest.sh Scripts/playtest/component-whole-path-walk.json --no-build, and look at path-6-three-copies-sc.png
anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task

log.note: Argued with the trade first. Printing the component name on every copy is the thing the 2026-09-08 width fix removed, and it is wrong for a UI tool: a screen made of twelve buttons would wear twelve identical labels, each wider than the button under it. Dropping the marker is also wrong: the diamond is the only thing on the canvas saying a drawing is a copy at all. So the name came back as something you summon.

Built: a component drawing spells out its whole identity while it is the one you are looking at (pointer resting on it, or picked) and goes back to its short word when you are not. A copy says "Save button"; a version says "Save button \u00b7 Disabled", which also gives the original back the component name the width fix took off it.

Exactly one drawing spells out at a time, and pointing beats having picked. First cut let hover and selection both bloom and two plates butted together reading "Primary \u00b7 Default" "Primary \u00b7 Off" as one long bar saying Primary twice, which is the very shape the short labels exist to avoid. A box selection would have printed it a dozen times.

Positions are still worked out from the RESTING captions, so nothing in the row moves when a name grows; the grown one draws last, on a plate, so it is the legible one where it overlaps. Panning and pinching now re-read what the pointer is on, so a name does not hang over a drawing that slid out from under it.

Core rule is in CanvasNameLabels.caption(isLive:) with tests (Tests/PhotonzCoreTests/CanvasNameLabelTests.swift, suite "The name on the drawing you are looking at"). App: CanvasNames.swift (chips, lookedAtComponent, spelledOutComponentID), CanvasComponents.swift (drawNameChip + plate), CanvasZoom.swift (re-read on pan/zoom).

Verified: Scripts/test.sh 5338 tests green. Walks re-run against a freshly built probe: 15 component walks, 6 version walks, 5 frame walks, all pass. path-6-three-copies-sc.png shows the picked copy reading "Save button" with the other two on bare marks; labels-5-hovered-sc.png (new stage on version-labels-row-walk) shows a hovered original reading "Primary \u00b7 Default" at 100% with none of the four labels covering another. At 50% the row is unchanged from the 2026-09-08 fix.
Audit queue/audits/2026-09-09-copy-names.json. Follow-up filed: the-field-that-opens-on-a-spelled-out-name-says (the rename box holds only the version while the label reads both words).

A component drawing spells out its whole name while it is the one you are looking at (pointer on it, or picked) and keeps its short word at rest, so a copy is never anonymous when you ask and a row of twelve never shouts.
